summary: @servicetitan/hammer-react preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated 727KB payload
details: The package declares `preinstall = node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers and per-function string-lookup dictionaries) and, when run on `npm install`, checks for a local `bun` binary and — if absent — downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts the platform-specific executable to a temp directory, chmods it 0755, and invokes it against the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB obfuscator.io-shape payload: rotated string/constant array (`n7gIxM`) with a rotator function (`WV8StW`) and a custom shuffled-base64 decoder (`hc1jfK9`), so its network/filesystem/credential behavior is only resolved at runtime, under a runtime that Node-based install-time inspection does not observe. The package is published as a React UI component library and has no functional reason to fetch an alternate JavaScript runtime at install time or to ship an obfuscated loader plus an obfuscated payload. The combination — obfuscated preinstall loader, install-time fetch of a runtime foreign to the package's stated purpose, and execution of an obfuscated blob under that runtime — is an alternate-runtime dropper pattern that hides install-time behavior from standard supply-chain review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
